description: Composite simulation figure (3D cellular-automaton output, mesoscale field maps) of a low-alloy steel, organised as three lettered groups (a)-(c), each containing two rows; every row is a left-hand simulated "Microstructure" map and a right-hand "Dislocation density" field map of the same YZ surface, each with a 100 µm scale bar and a 100 × 100 µm viewing frame. Panel (a): 0.4 strain with DRX fraction (frist: 28.3%; second: 10.1%) and 0.6 strain (frist: 29.4%; second: 58.2%); panel (b): 0.6 strain (frist: 86.9%; second: 6.5%) and 0.8 strain (frist: 53.3%; second: 43.5%); panel (c): 0.6 strain (frist: 88.6%; second: 7.9%) and 0.8 strain (frist: 57.4%; second: 40.5%). Colourbars are titled "Dislocation density (×10^14 m^-2)" for (a) and (b) (ranges 0.001-2.000 and 0.001-1.500) and "Dislocation density (×10^13 m^-2)" for (c) (0.01-3.5). Printed ρ intervals are given beneath every right-hand map: (a) 1×10^11-2.615×10^14 and 1×10^11-1.777×10^14 m^-2; (b) 1×10^11-1.233×10^14 and 1×10^11-1.126×10^14 m^-2; (c) 1×10^11-2.539×10^13 and 1×10^11-2.244×10^13 m^-2. A bottom legend reads "White grains: matrix  Green grains: first stage  Red grains: second stage".

subfigures.description: Two rows (0.4 strain and 0.6 strain) each pairing a simulated microstructure map with a dislocation-density map, 100 µm scale bars. Top row DRX fraction frist 28.3%, second 10.1%; bottom row frist 29.4%, second 58.2%. Colourbar 0.001-2.000 ×10^14 m^-2; ρ ranges 1×10^11-2.615×10^14 and 1×10^11-1.777×10^14 m^-2. The 0.6-strain row shows abundant red (second-stage) grains replacing white matrix.

Two rows (0.6 strain and 0.8 strain). Top row DRX fraction frist 86.9%, second 6.5%; bottom row frist 53.3%, second 43.5%. Colourbar 0.001-1.500 ×10^14 m^-2; ρ ranges 1×10^11-1.233×10^14 and 1×10^11-1.126×10^14 m^-2. Microstructure is dominated by green first-stage grains at 0.6 strain, with many red grains appearing at 0.8 strain and little white matrix left.

Two rows (0.6 strain and 0.8 strain) for the decreasing-temperature condition. Top row DRX fraction frist 88.6%, second 7.9%; bottom row frist 57.4%, second 40.5%. Colourbar 0.01-3.5 ×10^13 m^-2; ρ ranges 1×10^11-2.539×10^13 and 1×10^11-2.244×10^13 m^-2. A few dark, low-density second-stage grains appear inside first-stage grains already at 0.6 strain.

observations.observation: Each of the six rows pairs a left 'Microstructure' grain map with a right 'Dislocation density' field map of the same YZ surface, both stamped with a 100 µm scale bar.
A bottom legend defines the grain colour code: white grains = matrix, green grains = first stage, red grains = second stage.
Printed DRX fractions in (a) are frist 28.3% / second 10.1% at 0.4 strain and frist 29.4% / second 58.2% at 0.6 strain.
Printed DRX fractions in (b) are frist 86.9% / second 6.5% at 0.6 strain and frist 53.3% / second 43.5% at 0.8 strain.
Printed DRX fractions in (c) are frist 88.6% / second 7.9% at 0.6 strain and frist 57.4% / second 40.5% at 0.8 strain.
Dislocation-density colourbars are labelled ×10^14 m^-2 in (a) (0.001-2.000) and (b) (0.001-1.500), but ×10^13 m^-2 in (c) (0.01-3.5), i.e. panel (c) is an order of magnitude lower in density scale.

In the dislocation-density maps the highest values (red/orange) form thin networks along grain boundaries and around second-stage (red) grains, while grain interiors are blue (low density); the very highest maxima appear in panel (a) at 0.4 and 0.6 strain.

The caption states the strain rate was transiently increased from 0.01 s^-1 to 0.1 s^-1, at 0.2 strain for (a) and 0.4 strain for (b), under 950 °C, and that (c) corresponds to decreasing temperature from 1050 °C to 950 °C over a strain range of 0.4-0.5 at 0.01 s^-1.

The caption labels (a) as the 0.2-strain transient case and (b) as the 0.4-strain transient case, whereas the strain labels printed inside panels (a) and (b) read 0.4/0.6 strain and 0.6/0.8 strain respectively; the two readings do not match directly.
The citing text states that DRXGs_II first nucleate at the grain boundaries of the matrix because of greater distortion energy caused by dislocation density at 0.4 strain.
The citing text states that the average dislocation density of DRXGs_II is lower than that of both the matrix and DRXGs_I, providing the driving force for refinement.
The citing text states that at 0.6 strain the DRXGs_II begin to refine DRXGs_I (Fig. 23a), and that in Fig. 23b/23c the refinement mainly involves DRXGs_I because little residual matrix remains.

Panel (b) at 0.8 strain shows a largely green/red grain structure with almost no white matrix, consistent with the low residual-matrix statement, and its dislocation-density map is visibly bluer (lower density) than panel (a).

Second-stage (red) grains in every microstructure map are of comparable or larger size than first-stage (green) grains and lie at boundaries of green grains or matrix, indicating nucleation at existing boundaries.

unreadable_items: Caption vs printed label mismatch: caption places (a) at 0.2 strain and (b) at 0.4 strain, but the strain annotations inside the panels read 0.4/0.6 strain (a) and 0.6/0.8 strain (b); which strain the transient increase is illustrated at cannot be resolved from the image alone.
Individual grain boundaries within the dense green/red networks of (b) 0.8 strain and (c) are not separable at the supplied resolution, so exact grain counts cannot be made.
